title: Scandal, Associative Stigma, and Sorting in Labor Markets: Archival and Experimental Evidence
eligible_reason: Staffer-year panel (2000-2018) with binary post-scandal indicator switching on at the employer's scandal year, which varies across politicians (107 scandal-involved members per Table 2 log output); staffer FE plus calendar-year dummies; Table 4 columns 1 and 5 have no controls and Figure 2 is an unstacked event study without controls. Modern estimators (csdid, did_imputation, eventstudyinteract, stackedev) are reported in Appendix Figure C1 but all include time-varying covariates.
design_notes: Treatment: a congressional staffer's employer (member of Congress) is involved in a managerial-misconduct scandal; scand_post = post-scandal years. Outcome m_move_scandal_t = newly hired by an employer with a scandal. Sample: eventually-treated staffers (sample_treatments) and matched controls (sample_controls). Heterogeneity by scandal type (scandal_sex_crime: personal vs professional) via interactions. Experiments (SPSS) are separate.
estimators_reported: callaway_santanna (csdid, Appendix Fig C1a, with covariates)
borusyak_jaravel_spiess (did_imputation, Appendix Fig C1b, with controls)
sun_abraham (eventstudyinteract, Appendix Fig C1c, with covariates)
stacked (stackedev, Appendix Fig C1d, with covariates)

ineligible_specs_summary: Table 4 cols 2,6 add $covariates (avg_rate_salary_title, tenure_exp, year_relationship, number_politicians, ln_org_size, pol_maj: time-varying) -> excluded; cols 3,4,7,8 interact scand_post with scandal_sex_crime -> excluded. Appendix Figure C1 csdid/did_imputation/eventstudyinteract/stackedev all with covariates -> not eligible versions, but confirm the paper reports modern estimators.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Not computable without data; scandal years span 2000-2018 (year1-year18), 107 scandal-involved politicians (91 professional, 16 personal) per Table 2 output in Replication_log.txt, so multiple cohorts are certain.
data_files_note: Archival data (Legistorm congressional staffer employment records, 2000-2018) are under NDA and not shipped; only Replication_code.do and Replication_log.txt (Stata log of the original run through Table 6) are provided. Data files referenced: politician_panel.dta, compensation_person_year.dta, employer_study_*.dta, worker_study_*.dta. Experimental data (xlsx) and SPSS syntax are shipped but irrelevant.
software_note: Stata SE 18.5; reghdfe, coefplot, csdid, did_imputation, eventstudyinteract, stackedev.
screener_notes: No article text. Eligible design with two static TWFE specs (Table 4 cols 1 and 5) and one event study (Figure 2), but data require a Legistorm license or author cooperation. The cluster variable year_member_id yields 6,775 clusters on 38,357 obs, so it is likely member-by-year rather than member. The Figure 2 event study includes a full set of relative-time bins (pre, g_5..g_1, g0..g5, later) with no explicit omitted category; the exact definitions of 'pre' and 'later' are in the data, not the code.
